candidates.description:
Move method XsetIgnore to org.apache.tools.ant.taskdefs.MatchingTask
Rationale: The method XsetIgnore() is primarily concerned with processing a string of filenames and directory names to be ignored, which directly relates to the functionality of including and excluding files based on pattern matching. Since MatchingTask already contains methods for creating include and exclude patterns, moving XsetIgnore() to this class will enhance cohesion by grouping all related operations for managing file inclusions and exclusions in one place. Additionally, it will allow for better maintenance and understanding of the codebase, as all file-related operations will reside within MatchingTask.

candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method checkAndAddDependants to class GenericDeploymentTool
candidates.description:
Move method checkAndAddDependants to org.apache.tools.ant.taskdefs.optional.ejb.GenericDeploymentTool
Rationale: The method checkAndAddDependants() is primarily concerned with analyzing and adding class dependencies related to the EJB deployment process. Since this functionality directly interacts with the dependencyAnalyzer of the GenericDeploymentTool class and is essential for its operation, it is logical for this method to remain within the GenericDeploymentTool class. Moving it out would disrupt the encapsulation of functionality that is tightly coupled with the deployment process.

candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method createSupport to class Config
candidates.description:
Move method createSupport to org.apache.tools.ant.taskdefs.optional.ejb.EjbJar.Config
Rationale: The createSupport() method is responsible for creating and managing a FileSet for support elements, which directly interacts with the 'supportFileSets' list in the Config class. Since the primary purpose of the Config class is to maintain configuration state, including file sets related to the EJB jar task, it is logical for this method to reside within the Config class. Moving the method here enhances cohesion by ensuring that all operations related to file set management are encapsulated within the configuration context, thereby adhering to the Single Responsibility Principle.

candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method validateConfig to class Config

Move method validateConfig to org.apache.tools.ant.taskdefs.optional.ejb.EjbJar.Config
Rationale: The validateConfig() method is responsible for validating the configuration settings, which directly pertain to the attributes defined within the Config class, such as srcDir, descriptorDir, namingScheme, and baseJarName. Moving this method to the Config class aligns its functionality with the data it operates on, thereby adhering to the principle of encapsulation. This change will enhance the clarity of the codebase by ensuring that configuration-related logic resides within the configuration class itself, making it easier to manage and understand the validation rules associated with the configuration state.

candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method createDTD to class Config

Move method createDTD to org.apache.tools.ant.taskdefs.optional.ejb.EjbJar.Config

Since the Config class already holds a list of configured DTD locations (dtdLocations), it is logical for the method to reside here. Moving createDTD() to Config will enhance the cohesion of the class by ensuring that all methods related to configuration management, including DTD locations, are encapsulated within the same class. This will also improve maintainability and readability, as developers will find all configuration-related functionalities in one place.

candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method addDeploymentTool to class EJBDeploymentTool
candidates.description:
Move method addDeploymentTool to org.apache.tools.ant.taskdefs.optional.ejb.EJBDeploymentTool
Rationale: The method 'addDeploymentTool' is directly related to managing instances of deployment tools, specifically EJBDeploymentTool, as it adds them to a list and also sets the task associated with the deployment tool. This indicates that the method is fundamentally about the behavior and management of deployment tools themselves. Moving this method to the EJBDeploymentTool interface would encapsulate the functionality of adding and configuring deployment tools, making it more cohesive and aligned with the responsibilities of the deployment tools. This separation enhances maintainability and ensures that the deployment tools can manage their own configurations more effectively.

The method evaluates whether a file is selected based on the conditions defined in the IsFileSelected instance. Moving eval2() to IsFileSelected enhances cohesion, as it directly operates on the attributes and methods of the IsFileSelected class. Furthermore, it utilizes properties like 'file' and 'baseDir' from IsFileSelected, making it more intuitive for the method to reside within this class. Additionally, since eval2() is designed to validate and process the selection logic specific to file selection, it aligns better with the responsibilities of IsFileSelected, thereby improving the overall design and maintainability of the code.
